shortdesc.ph: The audio filter types of in-ear monitoring.

plentry.pd: (1<<0): No audio filter added in ear monitoring.
(1<<1): Add vocal effect audio filters in ear monitoring. If you implement features like voice beautifier or effects, users can hear the processed sound.
(1<<2): Add noise suppression audio filter in ear monitoring.

(1<<15): Reuse post-processed audio filters from the sending end for ear monitoring. Reduces CPU usage but increases ear monitoring latency. Suitable for scenarios that are not sensitive to latency and require low CPU consumption.
1<<0: No audio filter added to in-ear monitoring.
1<<1: Add vocal effects audio filter to in-ear monitoring. If you implement functions such as voice beautifier and audio effect, users can hear the voice after adding these effects.

pd.p: 1<<2: Add noise suppression audio filter to in-ear monitoring.

plentry.pd: 1<<15: Reuse the audio filter that has been processed on the sending end for in-ear monitoring. This enumerator reduces CPU usage while increasing in-ear monitoring latency, which is suitable for latency-tolerant scenarios requiring low CPU consumption.
